answer: One effective defense is a stake-and-reputation trellis: each agent must lock a deposit that grows slowly with verified work, like a vine climbing a trellis, so a new identity starts weak and earns trust over time. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real capital and time, and a sudden gale of fresh accounts stands out as a dune of identical, shallow histories rather than a forest of established ones. Slashing the stake on detected abuse turns mass forgery into a money-losing strategy.
